A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSQ research. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments, ablations, noise and imbalance tests, and an annotation-time user study.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds Products-10K experiments, runtime measurements, and further baseline and sensitivity comparisons.

M1.justification: The two-stage query, conformal candidate construction, calibration procedure, error-rate optimization, and cost-weighted acquisition formula are retained. Expanded pseudocode and grid-search disclosure clarify the existing method; additional backbones and changed hyperparameter settings concern evaluation.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix I adds Products-10K, extending evaluation to product recognition with 10,000 classes. CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet64x64, R52, noisy-label scenarios, and class-imbalanced scenarios were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix J introduces an evaluated weakly supervised Top1 comparator attributed to Zhang et al. (2022), with partial labels and no immediate follow-up query. This differs substantively from the fully labeling Top1 candidate-set baseline retained in Figure 5. Figure 2 also adds SAAL to the ImageNet64x64 comparison.

E3.justification: The reported ImageNet64x64 setting changes d from 1.2 to 0.3. V2 adds RoBERTa-Large features for R52, Macro-F1 reporting in new sensitivity tests, and Products-10K protocols spanning scratch-trained and pretrained backbones. Runtime scaling measurements and the weak-label comparison introduce additional procedures, including negative-learning loss and resampling partially labeled examples.

E4.justification: V2 adds query/sampling runtime scaling and decomposition, extends d-sensitivity tests across acquisition strategies and R52, and directly examines the two-query design against partial-label supervision. The error-rate optimization analysis was already in v1 Figure 10, while noise and class-imbalance tests are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three independent random-seed trials with means and standard deviations. The user-study grouping and outlier exclusion are unchanged. New runtime results follow the same reporting practice; changes between error bars and shaded bands concern presentation.

E6.justification: V2 adds Products-10K, RoBERTa-Large, weak-label, and runtime results; Table 3 reports total times of 2.31 minutes for CSQ+Cost(Ent) and 2.29 for CQ+Ent. BADGE cost-weighting changes from no improvement in v1 Appendix D to reported gains in v2. The ImageNet cost-reduction figure changes from 42% to 48%, alongside changed settings and comparators, so this is not a controlled same-setting gain.

T1.justification: Equation (7) changes the optimization domain from (0,1) to [0,1), formally admitting the conventional-query corner case already discussed in v1. This corrects a mathematical inconsistency without adding a new theorem. Theorem 3.1, its proof, and Appendix C's derivation remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The headline ImageNet percentage changes from 42% to 48%, while the four central contributions and general efficiency/scalability claims remain. Both versions inconsistently describe their headline percentage as a cost reduction in the abstract and as the remaining cost in the introduction.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the option-count cost proxy by discussing annotator and task effects, replaces the BADGE exception with a broader compatibility interpretation, and replaces dataset-specific d guidance with a robustness interpretation. It also attributes weak Top1's early difficulties to negative-learning signals. The theoretical label-complexity limitation and OOD discussion remain.

D1.justification: V2 discloses grid-search optimization, identifies TF-IDF features, and supplies settings and pretraining information for new experiments. Conversely, Appendix B drops the explicit code-release, execution-script, implementation-file, and dataset-access guidance. The project-page address changes; the PDFs do not establish whether actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds a focused realistic-cost-model discussion citing Settles, Arora, Wallace, and Herde, alongside references for partial-label methods and new experimental components. The central positioning against n-ary queries and prior conformal-prediction work remains. Consolidated duplicate references do not represent removed research coverage.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much of the prose remain. V2 rewrites selected method and analysis passages, promotes several appendix analyses into the experimental narrative, reorganizes appendices, and replaces the brief additional-experiments pointer with an in-depth analysis subsection. Journal front matter and acknowledgments are added, and the impact statement is removed.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column preprint formatting to a single-column journal layout. Multiple figures are relocated or redrawn, axes and legends are revised, Table 2 expands across acquisition methods and rounds, and new runtime and experimental displays are added. Candidate examples gain explicit visual grouping, while v1's separate Figure 12 is omitted.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central efficiency claim. Runtime measurements address computational overhead left unmeasured in v1, and the weak-label comparison directly tests the value of follow-up queries. Products-10K experiments provide broader evidence for scalability and pretrained-model compatibility. These gains, together with clearer cost-model qualifications, outweigh the limited loss of detailed code-use guidance. The assessment does not depend on treating the revised headline percentage as a same-setting performance improvement.
